about: Written by Claude from the Oct 9, 2026 annotated corpus. Narrative only. Every number shown on the site comes from running each item's `match` against data/annotated_reviews.csv in build_site_data.py. Tokens in text ({{count}}, {{pct_low_star}}, {{avg_rating}}, {{ios_count}}, {{android_count}}, {{pct_of_substantive}}) are filled from that item's own match. Each improvement, request, and strength also carries a `next` line: the check a PM would run, written by Claude, tokens filled the same way.

match_spec.labels_any: review has at least one of these labels
match_spec.categories_any: review has at least one of these categories
match_spec.categories_all: review has every one of these categories
match_spec.pattern: case-insensitive regex searched in lowercase title + review_text + english_translation + topic, joined by spaces
match_spec.regression_claim: true = only reviews with regression_claim TRUE
match_spec.competitors_any: review names at least one of these competitors

evidence_note: Store reviews are self-selected and skew to people who are delighted or angry. Treat everything here as a signal to investigate, not a validated problem or a market size.

callouts.title: The sharpest complaints are about money, not answers
callouts.text: {{count}} complaints and requests are about credits, free limits, pricing, or billing. {{pct_low_star}} of them come with 1 or 2 stars.

callouts.title: Accuracy is the largest single complaint
callouts.text: {{count}} reviews say answers were wrong, invented, or missed the question. Average rating {{avg_rating}}.

callouts.title: "It used to be better"
callouts.text: {{count}} reviewers say the product got worse than it was. {{ios_count}} of them are on iOS, far above iOS's share of the corpus.

callouts.title: Most reviews say nothing specific
callouts.text: Everything in Deep Dive and Opportunities rests on the reviews that name a feature, a problem, or a use case. The rest count toward volume and ratings only.

callouts.title: iOS is a small, angrier sample
callouts.text: Apple's feed returns at most 500 reviews per country, so iOS is thin here and US history starts Jul 29. Read platform comparisons with the review counts beside them.

improvements.title: Paying users run out of credits
improvements.desc: Subscribers say they hit a credit wall mid-task and are asked to buy more on top of a plan they thought covered everything. Many describe it as a bait and switch. Half of these reviews are on iOS.
improvements.next: Pull credit-balance telemetry for Pro users: what share reach zero before the cycle ends, and on which day. Then test showing the estimated cost before a run starts; the Run Receipt prototype shows one way.

improvements.title: Free tier stops at one photo or one image
improvements.desc: Free users hit the upload or image-generation cap on the first or second try, often before they've seen the feature work. Several say they can't judge whether Pro is worth it. Almost entirely Android.
improvements.next: Compare 7-day retention of free users who hit the photo cap in their first session against those who did not. If the capped cohort retains worse, test a higher first-week cap or show the limit before the upload.

improvements.title: Free question limits and upgrade prompts
improvements.desc: The app stops answering after a few questions and shows a payment screen. Reviewers compare this with free tiers elsewhere.
improvements.next: Measure time from install to the first paywall screen for free users, and that screen's conversion rate. If most free users hit it in their first session and few convert, the cap is a retention leak rather than a conversion lever.

improvements.title: Wrong or invented answers
improvements.desc: Wrong facts, made-up numbers, contradictions, and answers that have to be checked by hand. The most common complaint in the corpus.
improvements.next: Treat these {{count}} reviews as a seed eval set. Group them by failure type (invented fact, stale source, ignored instruction) and measure the current model on each group before deciding whether this is a retrieval or a model problem.

improvements.title: Doesn't follow what was asked
improvements.desc: The model misreads the question or ignores explicit instructions, even after the user repeats them.

match.pattern: ignor|misunderst|misread|not listen|doesn.t listen|did(n.t| not) understand|does(n.t| not) understand|instruction

improvements.next: These are the instruction-following slice of the eval set. Replay the exact pattern reviewers describe (an explicit instruction, repeated) against the current model and score it separately from factual accuracy.

improvements.title: Can't cancel, can't get a refund
improvements.desc: Users can't find how to cancel, are charged after cancelling, or report charges they didn't authorize. The lowest-rated cluster here.
improvements.next: Count cancel attempts that start in the app and end on a store support page. Add a visible cancel path that deep-links to the store subscription screen, and set a refund SLA. {{pct_low_star}} of these reviews are at 1 or 2 stars, so this is the cheapest rating gain on the page.

improvements.title: Partner offers that end badly
improvements.desc: Free Pro through a carrier, PayPal, or a phone maker that ends early, can't be cancelled, or turns into a charge.
improvements.next: List active partner promos and what happens when each ends. Add an end-of-promo notice before any charge, and check which partner generates most of these reviews.

improvements.title: Things that stopped working
improvements.desc: Crashes, freezes, cut-off responses, failed installs, and features that broke after an update.
improvements.next: Join these reviews to app version and device. The topics name failed updates and one device family, so if a single version or device dominates, this is a release or compatibility bug, not general instability.

improvements.title: Tone, bias, and refusals
improvements.desc: Answers described as rude, condescending, politically slanted, over-filtered, or far longer than the question needed.
improvements.next: Tag these by sub-type: tone, bias, refusal, length. Refusal and length are prompt and policy settings you can A/B test; tone and bias need a rubric eval before anything changes.

improvements.title: Voice mode and read-aloud
improvements.desc: Speech recognition misses words, the assistant talks over the user, voice cuts off, and read-aloud went missing for some.
improvements.next: Pull voice session logs for cut-offs and talk-over rate. Several reviews say read-aloud went missing, so check whether it was removed for a cohort or a platform.

improvements.title: Lost chats and lost context
improvements.desc: History disappears, long chats forget earlier turns, and threads can't be renamed or organized.
improvements.next: Measure how often long threads pass the context limit and how often history fails to load. Rename and folders are a steady request; confirm demand with usage of the existing bookmarks before building.

improvements.title: Support doesn't answer
improvements.desc: Billing and account problems that go unanswered or end with "nothing we can do".
improvements.next: Measure time to first human reply on billing tickets and the share closed without a resolution. Most of these overlap with cancel and refund reviews, so one support fix covers both.

improvements.title: Computer mode burns credits
improvements.desc: Reviews that mention Computer by name: tasks that drain credits before finishing, and being switched into it by default.
improvements.next: Measure credits per completed Computer task and the share of tasks that end at a zero balance. Show the estimate before the run and a stop point when a task will not finish on the remaining balance.

improvements.title: Model choice taken away
improvements.desc: Pro users say the model they pick isn't the one that answers, or that better models are now rationed.
improvements.next: Audit model routing: when a Pro user picks a model, log whether that model produced the answer. Where it did not, show the rule in the product instead of switching silently.

improvements.title: Forced sign-in and phone number
improvements.desc: Stuck at sign-in, locked out, or required to give a phone number to manage or cancel an account.
improvements.next: Count sign-in failures by provider, and remove the phone-number requirement from the cancel flow; reviews say it blocks cancellation outright.

improvements.title: "Why is this on my phone?"
improvements.desc: Android users who didn't install the app and resent it being there, plus permission and data-deletion worries.
improvements.next: Compare ratings and retention from preinstall channels (OEM and carrier) against organic installs. If preinstalled users rate lower, treat it as a channel problem and fix the first-open and uninstall paths, not the app.

feature_requests.title: More free photo and file uploads
feature_requests.desc: A higher daily cap, a few free image generations, or a reset that doesn't take a month.
feature_requests.next: Pair with the one-photo limit above: test a higher first-week upload cap and measure free-to-Pro conversion and 7-day retention, not complaint volume.

feature_requests.title: A trial, student, or regional price
feature_requests.desc: A free month to test Pro, student plans, and prices that fit local incomes.
feature_requests.next: These requests come from reviewers who still rate the app well. Test a student price and a regional price in two markets and read conversion and 90-day retention before rolling either out.

feature_requests.title: Deeper, fresher research
feature_requests.desc: More context in Deep Research, verified and current data, and better source handling.
feature_requests.next: Check Deep Research against the stated gaps: context length, freshness, and source handling. Each is measurable with the accuracy eval set.

feature_requests.title: Interface fixes
feature_requests.desc: Readable dark mode, text size, hiding follow-up suggestions, simpler navigation.
feature_requests.next: Small, concrete requests (dark mode contrast, text size, hiding follow-ups). Ship the cheapest two behind settings and watch whether the requests stop.

feature_requests.title: Better voice
feature_requests.desc: Read-aloud, hands-free and push-to-talk modes, more natural voices.
feature_requests.next: Hands-free and push-to-talk modes are the named asks. Check voice session length and drop-off before investing; voice complaints outnumber voice requests here.

feature_requests.title: Organize and keep chats
feature_requests.desc: Rename, folders, search, branching a conversation, memory that's understandable.
feature_requests.next: Rename, folders, and search over chats. Confirm with usage of existing bookmarks and history before building organisation features.

feature_requests.title: Agent features without the paywall
feature_requests.desc: Some automation or Computer use on lower tiers.
feature_requests.next: A request for Computer on lower tiers. Weigh it against the credit complaints above: wider access without a cost estimate would create more of those.

feature_requests.title: More models, more freely
feature_requests.desc: Specific models added, and fewer limits on switching.
feature_requests.next: Named model requests and fewer switching limits. Log which models users try to pick and are refused; that list is the roadmap.

strengths.title: Research is the reason people stay
strengths.desc: Praise that names research, in any language.
strengths.next: Keep research tasks in the regression eval. Any model or retrieval change ships only if research quality holds.

strengths.title: Sources and fresh information
strengths.desc: Citations, links, and up-to-date answers are the feature praised by name most often.
strengths.next: Sources are the stated reason to choose Perplexity. Treat citation accuracy as a guardrail metric and track citation click-through.

strengths.title: Students and homework
strengths.desc: Study, school, exams, and homework show up across languages.
strengths.next: Students are a named segment. Test the student price requested above against this group's retention.

strengths.title: Trusted answers
strengths.desc: Praise for accurate, reliable, precise answers. The same quality that draws the most complaints.
strengths.next: These reviews are the counterweight to the wrong-answer set. Use both as the eval baseline so a fix for one does not regress the other.

strengths.title: Fast
strengths.desc: Quick answers are a consistent point of praise.
strengths.next: Set a latency guardrail. Speed is praised by name, so a slower model has to prove it is worth the wait.

strengths.title: Many models in one app
strengths.desc: Paying once for access to several model families.
strengths.next: Protect the model bundle. The Model Choice complaints show when it breaks: a picked model that does not answer.

Generic Good: The largest group by far, and it carries the star average. It says the app is liked; it doesn't say why.
Mostly one to three words, in dozens of languages. Leave it out of any qualitative read.
Specific Praise: Accuracy, research and sources, everyday use cases like study, and speed cover most of it.
ChatGPT is the competitor named most often, in praise as well as in complaints.
Specific Complaint: Two different angry users: free users stopped by limits, and paying users stopped by credits.
Reviewers who say the product got worse point most often to accuracy, then to credits and free limits.
Billing and account complaints are the lowest-rated of all. They're operational, and fixable.
Feature Request: A small group, and friendlier than the complaints: most rate the app 4 or 5 stars.
Most requests ask for something that exists to be free or less limited, not for something new.
Generic Bad: Short dismissals with nothing to act on. Some name a competitor as better.
Nonsense: Off-topic text, test strings, and reviews that seem meant for another app. Excluded from sentiment reads.

category_notes.Answer Accuracy: The category with the most reviews, and it cuts both ways: heavy praise and the largest block of complaints.
category_notes.Search & Sources: Mostly praise. Sources and current information are what users name when they explain why they chose Perplexity.
category_notes.Answer Style & Filters: Clear explanations earn praise. Tone, bias, and refusals earn complaints.
category_notes.Model Choice: Praised as a bundle of models; criticized when the choice is limited or overridden.
category_notes.Credits & Paid Limits: Almost entirely complaints, and half of them on iOS. These are paying users.
category_notes.Free Limits & Paywall: The highest-volume pain point. Free users hit a wall early, most often on photos and images.
category_notes.Pricing & Value: Split between "too expensive" and requests for trials or cheaper tiers.
category_notes.Billing & Subscription: Cancellation, refunds, and unexpected charges. The lowest ratings in the corpus.
category_notes.Customer Support: Rarely the first problem, usually the second: an issue that support didn't resolve.
category_notes.Computer & Agents: A new surface with mixed reviews: impressive when it works, costly in credits when it doesn't.
category_notes.Voice & Dictation: Recognition errors, interruptions, and missing read-aloud.
category_notes.Images & Files: Mostly about limits on uploading and generating, less about quality.
category_notes.Threads & History: Lost history, lost context, and no way to organize chats.
category_notes.Bugs & Stability: Breakage after updates, failed installs, cut-off responses.
category_notes.Speed: Mostly praise for fast answers. Complaints are about slow responses and slow image generation.
category_notes.Login & Account: Sign-in loops, lockouts, and a phone-number requirement.
category_notes.UI / UX: Mostly praise for ease of use. Requests are small and concrete.
category_notes.Privacy & Permissions: Preinstalled-app resentment on Android, plus permission and data-deletion concerns.
category_notes.Use Cases: What people use it for: study, homework, work, daily questions. Nearly all positive.
category_notes.Other: Specific reviews that fit nowhere else: ads, language support, regional availability.
